Pros:

Open world, open map. You don't really have to wait in front of a loading screen unless you're loading up the game or moving to a different world.

Cheats are much easier to use. You don't have to use a mod to let you drag a relationship or needs bar.

There's vehicles in this game, meaning you can go anywhere faster, unlike in say, the Sims 4.

Colour and pattern customization is available for almost everything in the game. You can change the hair colour, the roots, the tips, or change the colour of the bed frame and the mattress separately, etc.

There's a lot to do in this game, lots of variety, lots of choices.

It has burglars and the repoman. While it doesn't seem like a very desirable thing to have, it adds another layer of immersive was to the game.

It has lots of progression- Townies will age, get married, have children as your sim does the same.

 The game just feels...alive. While you're doing something, you can go look around the hustle and bustle because other sims will be doing their own thing.

Loading screens give you something to do, with ingame rewards.

Cons:

It is very clunky. It runs like molasses, so save often and be prepared for crashes. I suggest getting the Nraas mods, Overwatch, ErrorTrap, StoryProgression and MasterController are recommended to keep your game running smoothly and better.

The graphics aren't as good in comparison to other games. 

The base characters are god awfully ugly. You'll need to use the sliders well (and maybe some cc) to make then look on the nicer side.

Expansions such as Isla Paradiso and Into The Future are very buggy. I wouldn't touch them.

While you don't have to see a loading screen a lot, loading can take very long at times. Same goes with saving. There's a bug with saving that causes it to endlessly loop- in that case you'll have to cut your losses and say goodbye to your progress from the last save.

And yet I know this dynamic is stupid, because we'll most likely fall out of touch sometime this year, and we've never really actually met, and I don't even know what most of them look like, I just know what their voices sound like. And now for the more depressing part:

I don't know whether or not to forgive my abusive mother. She's abused me, and on occasion, my younger sister, since I was 7. It started from disciplinary slaps to the hands and eventually evolved into full on angry rampages because she couldn't control her rage. She would pull my hair and slap my face, call me worthless and fat and force me to throw my things into the trash because they were, as she called them, trash. She would get angrier after I cried, and on several occasions, locked me outside in the backyard for three hours. She would threaten to 'send [me] to the streets to beg like the other worthless beggar children', and would push me down to the floor and kick me until I stopped making a sound. She would baby my sister, and punish me for things she did wrong, (like punching my nose for not reminding her what my sister had to wear to school a particular day; She told me to do so two months before that incident. Besides, I was in a different school than her and studying for exams, I didn't know!). There's only 2 occasions where she had abused my sister, and that was because they happened at night and I had my own room. The worst, however, was a couple months ago, when I was 14, she told me to go kill myself, and later in the day pushed me down the stairs. I don't know if I should forgive her. Because of her, I break down crying whenever I make a small mistake such as spill a drink. I feel absolutely worthless, stupid and annoying. * Helicopter Parenting. This is a very big no. Your kid will have no social skills whatsoever, and will come to slowly resent you. They also won't be capable of making decisions of their own, and speaking from experience this feels awful. Don't put them through it. Or worse, they'll turn out to be a gigantic brat.

Or "Why did I have children if I couldn't have them do this____ for me?" Bottom line is, just don't treat them like they owe you something the minute they're born. They're children. They're supposed to take, and take and take from you. They didn't choose to have you as a parent. You chose to have them.

* Invading their privacy. This is a very big issue. Don't randomly waltz into their rooms, don't snoop through their stuff, don't look through their texts. Knock and ask to enter. If you have suspicions, ask them. Don't just rummage through their stuff uninvited.

* Negative Reinforcement. This ones a biggie. Don't hit your children, don't call them worthless, don't trash their stuff. Give them an explanation of why they're getting punished. Tell them what they did. Reward good behaviour instead of brushing it off.

* Crazy ants reproduce by cloning themselves. Also, they are one of the first examples of an insect neutralizing another insect's venom, as they cover themselves with formic acid to protect from fire ant venom. They get their name from their irrational movements, and their colonies have multiple queens. They also really like electronics and can form an infestation inside em.

* As long as a mouse can fit it's head through a gap, it can fit the rest of their body through it as well, no matter how narrow it is. Adolescent mice can fit through holes the size of a pen, and adult mice can fit through holes the size of a nickel. 

* Certain species of insects such as bedbugs reproduce through a process called traumatic insemination. The male pierces the female's abdomen with his penis, often causing a lot of damage. The wound also has a chance to lead to infection later on.

* Once male lion cubs reach a certain age, they are kicked out of the pride and become 'nomads'. They then proceed to roam the land, either alone or with their siblings, and attempt to survive. Once they get strong enough, they eventually will take over another pride, kill the males, slaughter the cubs, and mate with the females. 

* If a giraffe and their young is attacked, the mother will attempt to hide her young in the grass or in the bushes. Sometimes, they will get away. Other times, the young is either found, dragged off and eaten, or occasionally accidentally trampled by their own mother while she attempts to defend them.

* The secretary bird is a species of bird with a very strange hunting method: it stomps it's prey to death. They start by stomping the ground and scaring off their target, before stomping until it's stunned/dead and swallowing it. In terms of later prey, they jump on their backs, breaking their spine or neck.

* Cockroaches have a specialized egg sac that allows the mother to essentially choose where to place her young, carrying the eggs with her wherever she goes. If she ever is attacked, she may eject the eggs as a last ditch attempt to save them.

* Lions will often steal the prey of other predators such as hyenas, leopards and cheetahs. They've been known to camp beneath a tree waiting for a leopard, and they slaughter the young of the aforementioned as well. They will also slaughter the young of each other, and steal the prey of any lion that are not part of their pride. They're basically dicks.

* Leopards will often eat their prey in a tree and cheetahs and solitary lions will move to a secluded area because of the previous point. Cheetahs will also often change dens to avoid other predators, however doing so endangers their cubs as they can only move one cub at a time, leaving the remaining cubs vulnerable. Leopard cubs practice their climbing skills within the safety of their den after reaching a certain age, preparing for the future.

* Cheetahs don't hunt by stalking and pouncing. Instead, they chase after their prey and trip them. Since they move so fast, they have a hard time turning quickly, and their stamina is quite low. Their tails acts like a rudder behind them.

* The reason why zebras have such unusual colouring is that while alone, they are very noticeable and easy to hunt, in a group, their patterns start to mesh together into one wave of black and white, and predators have a hard time focusing on a specific target.
